title: Animal bite: rabies post-exposure prophylaxis (India, NCDC)
subject: infectious-disease
summary: Categorise the exposure, wash every wound with soap and running water for 15 minutes, vaccinate for Category II and III (ID 0.1 mL at 2 sites on days 0, 3, 7, 28, or IM on days 0, 3, 7, 14, 28), and infiltrate rabies immunoglobulin (ERIG 40 IU/kg or HRIG 20 IU/kg) into all Category III wounds. Start at once, whatever the delay.

sections.title: Assess the exposure
items: Category I: touching or feeding animals, licks on intact skin. Wash the area; no PEP if the history is reliable.
Category II: nibbling of uncovered skin, minor scratches or abrasions without bleeding. Wound care plus vaccine.

Category III: single or multiple transdermal bites or scratches, licks on broken skin, saliva contamination of mucous membranes. Wound care plus rabies immunoglobulin plus vaccine. Any bleeding wound is Category III.
All wild animal bites and all bites in forest areas are Category III. Domestic rats, hares and rabbits do not ordinarily need PEP; bat exposure does not warrant PEP in India.
Give PEP regardless of the animal's vaccination status, whether the bite was provoked, or how late the patient presents (months later still counts). Start PEP at once; do not wait to observe the dog.

sections.title: Wound care (every exposure)
items: Wash and flush every wound and scratch immediately with soap and running water for 15 minutes; rinse exposed eyes and mucosa with water. Do it even if the patient presents late.
Then apply a virucidal antiseptic such as povidone-iodine or alcohol. Do not apply chillies, oil, turmeric, lime, soil or herbs; if already applied, wash them off gently.
Avoid primary suturing. If unavoidable, infiltrate RIG first, wait several hours, then place minimal loose sutures. Severe wounds: daily dressing and delayed secondary closure.
Tetanus prophylaxis as per the tetanus protocol; give an antibiotic course where the wound needs one.

sections.title: Rabies immunoglobulin (Category III)
items: Indication: every Category III exposure, and Category II exposures in immunocompromised patients. Not needed if the patient has documented complete PrEP or PEP (may be considered if direct nerve exposure is suspected).
Dose: ERIG 40 IU/kg or HRIG 20 IU/kg body weight; these are maximum doses. No skin test is required before ERIG; observe for 15 to 20 minutes afterwards with adrenaline available.

Infiltrate the whole calculated dose, or as much as anatomically possible without causing compartment syndrome, into and around all wounds. Fingertips, toes, ears, nose and genitalia can be infiltrated gently, avoiding excessive pressure.
Severe or multiple wounds: if the calculated volume is too small to reach every wound, dilute it 2 to 3 fold with sterile normal saline so that all wounds are infiltrated. Do not cut the dose.

Leftover RIG does not need to be injected IM at a distant site (WHO 2018); unused RIG can be used the same day for another patient if handled aseptically. Never inject RIG into the gluteal region, never IV, never in the same syringe as vaccine and never at the vaccine site.
Give RIG with the first vaccine dose or as soon as possible afterwards; it is not indicated beyond day 7 after the first vaccine dose.

Rabies monoclonal antibodies (DCGI-licensed products) are a WHO-endorsed alternative to RIG. The 2019 national guideline has not yet incorporated them; if used, dose by the product label (IU/kg differs between products) and infiltrate like RIG.

sections.title: Vaccine schedules (Category II and III)
items: Intradermal (Updated Thai Red Cross, preferred by NRCP): 0.1 mL at each of 2 sites (both deltoids) on days 0, 3, 7 and 28. Use only DCGI-approved ID vaccines; use an opened vial within 6 hours, stored at 2 to 8°C.
Intramuscular (Essen): 1 full vial IM in the deltoid (anterolateral thigh in infants and young children) on days 0, 3, 7, 14 and 28. Never in the gluteal region.
Same number of injections and dose per injection at every age and body weight.

Give the first 3 doses (days 0, 3, 7) within 10 days. A delay of 1 to 2 days does not require restarting; continue the schedule. Avoid switching route or brand, but if unavoidable continue without restarting.
Use the IM route in patients on chloroquine or hydroxychloroquine, long-term steroids or other immunosuppressants.

sections.title: Special situations
items: Pregnancy, lactation, infancy, old age and concurrent illness are not contraindications; give full PEP.

Immunocompromised (HIV, chemotherapy, long-term steroids): RIG for both Category II and III, full IM vaccine course, and check neutralising antibody 14 days after the course (adequate if 0.5 IU/mL or more).

Re-exposure after documented complete PEP or PrEP: wound care, no RIG, and 1-site ID (0.1 mL) or 1 full IM vial on days 0 and 3. Within 3 months of a complete course, wound washing alone suffices. Previous nerve tissue vaccine: give full PEP.

Dog or cat that stays healthy for 10 days of observation: an IM course can be converted to PrEP by omitting the day 14 dose and giving day 28; an ID course must be completed. The 10-day rule does not apply to other animals.
Close contacts of a human rabies patient exposed to secretions may be offered PEP as a precaution.

sections.title: Pre-exposure prophylaxis
items: Offer to laboratory staff, clinicians caring for rabies patients, veterinarians, animal handlers, dog catchers and wildlife staff; IAP suggests PrEP for children on a voluntary basis.
Schedule: IM 1 full vial, or ID 0.1 mL at 1 site, on days 0 and 7, with a third dose on day 21 or 28.
High-risk workers: check neutralising antibody every 6 months for the first 2 years, then every 2 years; boost if below 0.5 IU/mL.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Waiting to see whether the dog dies before starting PEP.
Omitting RIG in Category III exposures, or injecting it into the gluteal muscle instead of the wounds.
Suturing a bite wound before RIG infiltration.
Restarting the whole course after a missed dose.
Adding extra diluent to a vial to stretch ID doses (never do this).

drugs.name: Equine rabies immunoglobulin (ERIG)
drugs.dose: 40 IU/kg body weight, once, infiltrated into and around wounds
drugs.notes: Category III (and Category II if immunocompromised). Maximum dose; dilute 2 to 3 fold with normal saline if needed to reach all wounds. Never gluteal. Not beyond day 7 of vaccination.

drugs.name: Human rabies immunoglobulin (HRIG)
drugs.dose: 20 IU/kg body weight, once, infiltrated into and around wounds
drugs.notes: Maximum dose; dilute with normal saline if needed to reach all wounds. Never IV, never gluteal, never at the vaccine site.

drugs.name: Cell culture rabies vaccine, intradermal
drugs.dose: 0.1 mL ID at each of 2 sites on days 0, 3, 7 and 28
drugs.notes: DCGI-approved ID vaccine (potency 2.5 IU or more per IM dose). Same dose at all ages.

drugs.name: Cell culture rabies vaccine, intramuscular
drugs.dose: 1 full vial IM on days 0, 3, 7, 14 and 28
drugs.notes: Deltoid; anterolateral thigh in infants. Never gluteal.

drugs.name: Rabies vaccine, re-exposure
drugs.dose: 0.1 mL ID at 1 site, or 1 vial IM, on days 0 and 3
drugs.notes: Documented complete PEP or PrEP; no RIG needed.

drugs.name: Rabies vaccine, PrEP
drugs.dose: 1 vial IM or 0.1 mL ID at 1 site on days 0 and 7, and day 21 or 28

drugs.name: Rabies monoclonal antibody
drugs.dose: Per product label (IU/kg differs by product), infiltrated like RIG
drugs.notes: WHO-endorsed RIG alternative; not yet in the 2019 national guideline.

sources.title: WHO Expert Consultation on Rabies: third report (TRS 1012)
